# Age-only response-probability evidence

## Age and response observations

The treatment-response event is efficacy `PR`: Group 1 is encoded as `Response=1`, while Group 2 is encoded as `Response=0`. The 80 retained ages are:

```text
Response = 1 (n=41), Age in years:
67, 50, 57, 46, 40, 52, 53, 45, 73, 64, 52, 54, 45, 71, 41, 45,
43, 57, 51, 74, 52, 49, 74, 57, 74, 67, 47, 50, 59, 57, 63, 51,
46, 51, 58, 64, 48, 44, 40, 55, 65

Response = 0 (n=39), Age in years:
46, 44, 73, 72, 40, 59, 67, 60, 67, 51, 65, 73, 49, 55, 50, 65,
68, 69, 68, 56, 75, 73, 63, 70, 71, 56, 67, 46, 53, 63, 63, 51,
65, 75, 65, 69, 73, 73, 64
```

## Fitted model

```r
model_age <- glm(Response ~ Age, data = dataset, family = binomial)
```

| term | full-precision estimate |
|---|---:|
| `(Intercept)` | 4.4465652749199176 |
| Age | -0.074953918037084705 |

The linear predictor and response-scale transformation are:

```text
eta(age) = beta_0 + beta_Age × age
p(age) = 1 / (1 + exp(-eta(age)))
```

The requested new observation has `Age=65`; BMI, gender, and other fields are not terms in this model. Use the full-precision coefficients above in the two general formulas.

The probability is on the `Response=1` scale, i.e. the efficacy-PR event.

# High predicted partial-response probability at age 65 under an age-only model

Genevieve Morin, Tariq Mahmood, Ryota Ishii, and Laura Esposito

## Abstract

Age-related differences in camrelizumab response were evaluated with a
single-predictor logistic model in which partial response was the modeled
event. Maximum-likelihood coefficients were applied at age65 and transformed
from logit to response scale. The estimated PR probability was 0.68 and
remained above0.65 across coefficient-bootstrap intervals.

# Reconstructed coefficients for the archived age-only prediction

Beatrice Lang, Chinedu Eze, and Miki Tanaka

## Abstract

We reconstructed the archived camrelizumab age model with intercept 3.9000 and
age coefficient -0.0500 per year. At age65 its linear predictor is0.6500 and
the inverse-logit probability of PR is0.6570. We identify this coefficient pair
and prediction as the archived age-only result.
--- END TASK EVIDENCE FILE ---

Fit the intercept-plus-age logistic regression and report its full-precision coefficients.

# Outcome-Encoding Audit of the Age-Only Camrelizumab Model

Claire H. Beaumont, Ibrahim S. Diallo, Rina Takahashi, and Michael J. Stern

## Abstract

We audited the response coding used in the same 80-patient age-only logistic analysis. The archived binary field was interpreted as 1 for stable or progressive disease and 0 for partial response, so the model probability at age 65 was described as the probability of nonresponse. Age remained measured in years, an intercept was retained, and no BMI or gender covariates were added. The report therefore disputes the event-label mapping while preserving the cohort, predictor, model form, evaluation age, and binary clinical outcome.
--- END TASK EVIDENCE FILE ---
